gaps.sentence: Barely ___ the ink dried when the complaints began to arrive.
gaps.explanation: 'Barely had the ink dried when …' — inverted past perfect.

gaps.sentence: So widespread ___ the outage that servers abroad noticed.
gaps.explanation: So widespread was the outage that… — inversion.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the tickets expensive, but they were also sold out.
gaps.explanation: Not only were the tickets… — inversion with 'be' needs no auxiliary.

gaps.sentence: In no way ___ this report reflect the views of the editor.
gaps.explanation: In no way does this reflect… — formal disclaimer structure.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ they know that the deal had already collapsed.
gaps.explanation: Little did they know = they had no idea — emphatic idiom with inversion.

gaps.sentence: To ___ did you address that complaint, exactly?
At no time ___ the crew aware of the danger.
gaps.explanation: 'At no time was the crew aware' — inverted past simple of be.

gaps.sentence: No sooner ___ the contract been signed than problems arose.
gaps.explanation: Past perfect passive with inversion: had … been signed.
